communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: RCH 8.18.26
communications.communication:
Dear FOIA Officer:

You are receiving this correspondence as a request under the Freedom of Information Act, 5 U.S.C. subsection 552. I am requesting the following:

Copies of all Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) records, documents, and communications responsive to Raymond Charles Horsch, aka R. C. Hörsch, aka Stanley E. Stokowski, aka Richard Harris (May 5, 1943 – May 2025) through May 2025.

Mr. Horsch was a pornographic filmmaker and photographer, criminal forger, and drug trafficker. Mr. Horsch passed away in May 2025 from chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Although there is no obituary, his death was reported by the Philadelphia Inquirer in a June 27, 2026 article: https://www.inquirer.com/news/olney-raid-missing-women-mystery-drugs-20260627.html

Mr. Horsch is currently the subject of intense public interest due to a series of articles in the Philadelphia Inquirer reporting his connection to missing women in the Kensington section of Philadelphia. Articles referencing Mr. Horsch  can be found below:

https://www.inquirer.com/news/olney-raid-missing-women-mystery-drugs-20260627.html
https://www.inquirer.com/news/raymond-horsch-olney-missing-women-psych-exam-20260903.html
https://www.inquirer.com/crime/raymond-horsch-woman-killed-snuff-film-olney-20260828.html

As Mr. Horsch is the subject of multiple active investigations, I am requesting no records generated by the FBI after May 2025. Please only process records on or before that date.

I am asking you waive any fees associated with this request. I am a member of the news media. My bylines, which include Unicorn Riot, Covert Action Magazine, and the Geopolitical Economy Report, can be found in both print and electronic publications, and I am sending this request in coordination with Muckrock, an award-winning and nationally-recognized news organization. Please take note of the Office of Management and Budget guidelines published March 27, 1987 (52 FR 10012) that include electronic publications and other nontraditional publishers as representatives of the news media.

A fee waiver is appropriate in situations where "disclosure of the requested information is in the public interest because it is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of the operations and activities of the government, and is not primarily in the commercial interest of the requester,” 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(4)(iii). Mr. Horsch made statements to podcaster Ashley West on his Rialto Report podcast indicating that, during the early 1960s, he worked as an independent contractor for the Central Intelligence Agency, via the Wackenhut Corporation. In the course of this work, Mr. Horsch alleged that he carried out thefts and electronic surveillance on the behalf of the CIA and Wackenhut; he cited former Philadelphia district attorney James C. Crumlish, Jr. as one of his targets.

An archived copy of that discussion can be found here: https://web.archive.org/web/20210122022557/https://www.therialtoreport.com/2013/12/15/ray-horsch/

As Mr. West appears to have deleted the original episode, a newer version can be found here: https://www.therialtoreport.com/2026/09/13/ray-horsch-2/

Given Mr. Horsch's statements regarding work surveilling politicians for a federal agency, any records generated by the FBI about Mr. Horsch during his life would contribute significantly to public understanding of the operations and activities of the government.

This request is not being made for commercial purposes. All documents will be provided to the general public without charge.

Known aliases for Mr. Horsch include R. C. Hörsch, Stanley E. Stokowski, and Richard Harris. Please conduct a search of the Central Records System, including but not limited to the Electronic Surveillance (ELSUR) Records System, the Microphone Surveillance (MISUR) Indices, the Physical Surveillance (FISUR) Indices, and the Technical Surveillance (TESUR) Indices, for both main-file records and cross-reference records related to all known aliases for Mr. Horsch and the Wackenhut Corporation.

In the event that there are fees, I am willing to pay up to $100. Please advise if fees will exceed this amount so I might make an arrangement for requesting the records. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

I look forward to your response within 20 working days, as the statute requires. If access to the records I am requesting will take longer, please contact me with information about when I might expect copies or the ability to inspect the requested records.

If you deny any or all of this request, please cite each specific exemption you feel justifies the refusal to release the information and notify me of the appeal procedures available to me under the law.

Sincerely,

Robert Skvarla, Jr.
